source:
Create a high-speed, arcade-style speedrun game where players move at super-speed and have an electric dash ability.

Build 3 distinct levels connected linearly:

Level 1: A neon cyberpunk highway with moving grid walls, glowing laser beams to jump over, and high-speed booster pads.

Level 2: A futuristic factory with rotating electric rollers, timed vertical laser gates, and toxic waste pits.

Level 3: A crumbling space station with floating platforms that disappear 1 second after touch, and swinging electric pendulums.

Core Mechanics to Include:

Super-Speed: Set player default walk speed to 40.

Electric Dash: Press 'Q' or 'E' to instantly burst forward with an electric particle trail.

Coin System: Scatter spinning, glowing gold coins across all levels. Give coins a spinning animation script. Collectible coins must add +1 to a global 'Coins' leaderboard and play a ding sound.

Shop System: Add a basic UI menu button labeled 'Shop' where players can spend coins on trail effects.

Kill Hazards: Any contact with lasers or electric obstacles instantly resets the player to the nearest checkpoint.

Checkpoints: Place glowing green pad checkpoints at the start of every new level section
this should be 3d

answers.ask: How long should each of the three levels run? At walk speed 40 a course crosses ground four times faster than the usual baseline.
answers.answer: Make each level a compact 45–60 second run at the intended super-speed, with a few clearly spaced obstacle sections and checkpoints.

answers.ask: Are the three levels one continuous course or three separate maps joined by a teleport?
answers.answer: Build them as one continuous linear 3D course, with each themed level flowing directly into the next.

answers.ask: Is there a timer or a finish line the run is scored against?
answers.answer: Add a finish line at the end of Level 3 and a simple run timer so players can race for faster completion times.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] scale — Q: How long should each of the three levels run? At walk speed 40 a course crosses ground four times faster than the usual baseline. A: Make each level a compact 45–60 second run at the intended super-speed, with a few clearly spaced obstacle sections and checkpoints.
- [author] shape — Q: Are the three levels one continuous course or three separate maps joined by a teleport? A: Build them as one continuous linear 3D course, with each themed level flowing directly into the next.
- [author] goal — Q: Is there a timer or a finish line the run is scored against? A: Add a finish line at the end of Level 3 and a simple run timer so players can race for faster completion times.

## Enriched image prompt
Create one continuous high-speed 3D point-to-point course divided linearly into three distinct 45–60-second themed levels. Level 1 is a neon cyberpunk highway with moving grid walls and glowing laser beams to jump. Level 2 flows directly into a futuristic factory with rotating electric rollers, timed vertical laser gates, and toxic-waste pits. Level 3 continues into a crumbling space station with floating platforms that disappear one second after touch and swinging electric pendulums, ending at a clear finish line. Space every obstacle section for movement at speed 40 plus forward dashes, preserve safe landings between hazards, and keep the transitions continuous rather than using teleports or separate maps.

## Genre
The dominant genre is Obby & Platformer because discrete jumps, timed platforms, and moving obstacles define the run. Racing is secondary because the one-way course is timed from a start to a finish.

## Shape and preset
Use `route-point-to-point`, named Point to Point, from outside Obby's usual shapes: one route starts in Level 1 and ends after Level 3. The preset is Classic Obby, substituting the explicit point-to-point shape while retaining sequential track, checkpoints, jumping, and moving obstacles.

## Config requirements
Use `path-track` for the continuous physics-valid route through all three levels. Use `obstacle-jump` for highway lasers and station platform gaps, `obstacle-moving` for grid walls, electric rollers, laser gates, and pendulums, `obstacle-timing` for platforms disappearing one second after touch, and `hazard-kill` for lasers, electric obstacles, toxic waste, and the space-station void. Use the visible sides of `checkpoint-respawn`, `startpoint-line`, and `trigger-finish` for glowing green pads, the Level 1 start, and the Level 3 finish.

## Layout requirements
Place exactly three `checkpoint-respawn` pads, one at the start of each level, returning failed players to the nearest pad. Place one `startpoint-line` at Level 1 and one `trigger-finish` at the end of Level 3. Use `collectible-nodes` for spinning gold coins across all three levels and `powerup-buffs` for high-speed booster pads in Level 1, keeping both off impossible hazard lines.

## Layout components
The continuous container route has three zone segments. Neon Highway is a flat linear course with grid walls and laser jumps. Futuristic Factory is an enclosed sequence of roller, gate, and waste-pit sections. Crumbling Space Station is an open-air platform route with timed surfaces and swinging pendulums. Each segment lasts 45–60 seconds at intended speed and joins the next directly.

## Render order
Use `authored_plan`: the supported point-to-point route must be computed first so all three level segments connect and every speed-40 obstacle sequence remains clearable.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
The scale band is large, driven by three continuous 45–60-second high-speed sections while obstacle details remain readable. The theme progresses from neon cyberpunk highway to electric factory to crumbling space station. Use `P6` for the valid route and obstacle spacing, `P3` for crossing into enclosed factory and station spaces, and `CHECK` for open-air movement among the floating station platforms.
